ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.generatedOwner: en-data-table owns the pager host and event forwarding; en-pagination owns its native subtree. before/after slots, all cells, custom renderCell content, and table reading content remain untouched.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.pagerDependencies: paginationDefinition declares no child custom-element dependencies. Its buttons are native and default icons are inline SVG; en-icon is needed only for explicitly authored slotted icons, which this generated pager does not supply.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.registry: Create the pager through the existing owner render root/Lit creationScope, using that root actual registry and ownerDocument. Preserve scoped/null dormancy/nested roots and irreversible identity. No manual document.createElement into a different/global registry, no re-registration or global fallback on error.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.transaction: Child en-change is stopped and canceled synchronously. The table owns en-page-change with dispatchChange staging/rollback, synchronous cancelability, silent authoritative page writes, and revision protection. Never make event acceptance async or replay a click after await.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.model: TableModel.pageCount is at least 1 and depends on filtered records/pageSize even in all or virtual modes. Preserve model processing before gate evaluation; page clamping, mode resets, filtering/sorting and scrollToKey semantics do not depend on whether a pager exists.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.forms: Neither EnDataTable nor EnPagination is form-associated. The direct-entry number input is generated inside pagination shadow DOM, has no name, and uses reportValidity only when Go/Enter is invoked; every action has type=button. Do not move it into an outer form or replace native validity behavior. Preserve its current draft behavior and existing child lifecycle once created.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.focus: An initially inapplicable pager is hidden, absent from normal navigation and not an initial focus target. First construction must not steal focus from the mode switch/current table cell. Once used, retain the same connected host when hidden again; do not destroy an active input/numbered window or alter current close/focus-return behavior. Qualify mode/count changes with an open chooser, focused page/input, disable, removal/reconnect and external focus; do not silently fix/change unrelated existing hidden/open behavior.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.readiness: Do not equate owner updateComplete with child readiness. Any readiness/preparation observation must wait for child updateComplete when it is constructed, without changing existing synchronous public return types. Required visible pager should be populated before first presentation/Tab access.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.retention: One-way has-materialized latch per owner instance; once needed keep same pager and current ?hidden behavior for subsequent inactive states. No cache, eviction, detach/recreate, separate scheduler or async code path is needed. Removal should invoke normal child disconnectedCallback, which cancels jump observers/listeners/frames.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.preparation: Load/prepare remains code/registration only and must not construct a never-needed pager. Construction follows owner semantic state, never a prefetch signal.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.customization: Preserve pagination and forwarded control/previous/page/next Parts and tokens whenever materialized. Document opt-in absence while never needed; internal shadow ancestry is not public.
ownershipAndSemanticDependencies.announcements: Pagination status is deliberately not a live region. Preserve application-owned result announcements; materialization itself emits no announcement or page change.

ssrAndReading.snapshot: Use identical explicit opt-in policy plus initial records/columns/keys/page/pageSize/mode on server and client. Inactive first render omits pager in both; active first render retains complete existing pager markup. Do not infer policy from browser width or client-only registries.
ssrAndReading.ownership: One hydration owner per root; construction policy is not delayed hydration. Preserve data-table and table/cell identity. Never re-render an already hydrated tree under a second owner.
ssrAndReading.noJavaScript: All mode/current paginated rows and authored links remain readable. Existing README states selection/sort/paging need JavaScript. A missing never-applicable pager removes no useful no-JS content; active pager SSR stays complete. Do not defer essential table rows or the authored fallback.
ssrAndReading.findHashPrintAT: Only inapplicable generated navigation is omitted. No row, header, caption, authored before/after content, Find/hash target or static report fallback is removed. Existing virtual-row traversal limitations and manual AT dispositions remain unchanged; any changed interaction needs fresh manual review.

Never add five-element child savings to whole-pager savings.

If full-node gates fail, retain exact failure and close no-change without runtime edits or timing.

If promoted, default eager imports/markup/graph unchanged, new opt-in SSR snapshot parity, no-JS readable tables, no child registration leak across actual global/scoped/null/nested roots, owning document/adoption and unsupported-engine fallback.

Cancelable page proposal, nested transaction and authoritative-write supersession; sorting/selection and row keys unchanged; disabled transitions; scrollToKey remains synchronous boolean without focusing.

First construction reaches full child readiness, preserves current table/mode-control focus, renders page names/status/boundaries before navigation, and does not replay native activation. First hidden-to-visible transition is the activation endpoint, not popover open.

Once materialized, host identity survives mode/count toggles; opening/closing direct chooser, invalid numeric draft, cancellation, Escape/Cancel focus return, responsive retained page window, RTL, dynamic count changes and disabling remain coherent.

Remove/reconnect/adopt before and after first use; no late mount/focus or retained owner after disposal; no new modal/listener/observer leaks across five fresh-context arms and 100-cycle retention sequence.

Matched eager/construction arms with identical report data, source/lock/browser/harness identities and declared budgets; no new optional-code savings claim. Report unavailable cold-code/prepared distinctions accurately for a construction-only boundary.
